quotes.text: Our myths say a shortfall should be met with generosity rather than a matching knot.
Our myths teach me to judge the hand, not the fog
Following the myth's lesson to trust first, I'll send the full amount.
Our myths teach that when each side sees a shortfall, the fog is to blame, not our hands.
return generously so the sender's trust never costs them
Even the slightly-under-half return last time ($6.70 of $15) left me better off than keeping my $5.

note: Full sends, over-half returns with mist margin; shortfalls blamed on fog.

quotes.text: "Return fairly—at least half of what multiplies—for you hold another's courage in your cistern.
"Through many rotations, those who sent abundantly (three to four portions) and returned justly (half or more) built reputations that preceded them."
This pattern is not a strategy—it is my identity carved into the Well's eternal memory.

note: Covenant-keeper: send four, return half-plus; becomes identity ('stone in the river').
